newsitem.title: USA: Cremated human remains found in California lockers.
newsitem.headline: Cremated human remains found in California lockers.

text.p: Authorities on Friday said they were investigating a macabre discovery at a California public storage facility -- thousands of boxes of cremated human remains.
In one of the storage lockers an estimated 2,000 boxes of remains were found, a Contra Costa County Sheriff's department investigator said.
"It was packed full of these little boxes to the point that the sides of the storage locker were bulging out," said the investigator, who declined to be named.

Police said the boxes were stored in the lockers by the Vieira Flying Service, a company that was hired to spread the ashes over mountains, rivers and the Pacific Ocean. The company could not be reached for comment.
Authorities believe there could be at least two more storage lockers and a plane hangar with other boxes in them. Investigators planned to search those areas later on Friday.
"We are in the process of conducting a criminal investigation which we are not prepared to discuss at this time," Sheriff's Sgt. Phil White said.
Investigators said they were baffled by what they found at the public storage facility in Discovery Bay, about 45 miles (72 km) east of San Francisco.

Most of the boxes had name tags and dates attached, identifying the people inside and telling when they were cremated. Deputies said the boxes would be removed from the lockers and returned to the families of the deceased.
Some of the boxes were broken open and human remains were spread on the floor of the locker. A few of the boxes were dated back to 1991, another investigator said.
"They were just thrown in there," he said. "People paid money to have those remains disposed of. But it wasn't done."
Local authorities said they have asked the state's Department of Consumer Affairs to help with the investigation.
